prayerExcerpt.en-US: Our Lord said to St. Gertrude, "God accepts every soul you set free, as if you had redeemed him from captivity, and will reward you in a fitting time for the benefit you have conferred."
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Nosso Senhor disse a Santa Gertrudes: "Deus aceita cada alma que libertas, como se a tivesses resgatado do cativeiro, e te recompensará no tempo devido pelo benefício que conferiste."

meta.face: An Irishman of about fifty with a fair, fresh, lightly ruddy complexion and a smooth, UNLINED, OVAL face somewhat LONGER than wide — a high, ROUNDED forehead, a SHORT, straight nose with a slightly UPTURNED, neat tip, LARGE, clear, grey-blue eyes set WIDE apart, their lower lids lifted by a quiet smile, soft, arched brown brows, FIRM, smooth cheeks, a small, calm, closed mouth turned up at the corners, a SMALL, rounded chin; CLEAN-SHAVEN; brown hair greying a little, cut short in a Roman round tonsure; the gaze grave but joyful. Not the broad, white-haired, Irish-tonsured columba, the long, flaxen finbarr, the heart-shaped fiaker, the square, snub-nosed gall, the big-boned columban, the long, handsome oswald_worcester, or the clean-shaven, beak-nosed wilfrid.
meta.basis: No likeness survives. St. Bernard's Life of St. Malachy (tr. Lawlor, 1920, `bernard-malachy.txt`) says that 'neither did sadness darken nor laughter turn to levity the joyousness of his countenance' and that even in death his brow was not wrinkled nor his face wasted: hence a smooth, serene, gently smiling face.
